findings.claim: 'For 12-mark Discuss questions, develop both sides fully'
findings.truth: The 12-mark (d) question on this paper uses the command word Evaluate. Discuss is another board's wording.
findings.evidence: spec Appendix 3 command-word table (Evaluate, 12 marks, AO2)

findings.claim: Question 2 is typed '3 marks - Describe'
findings.truth: Each of the two questions runs (a) 3-mark Outline three, (b) 4-mark Explain two, (c) 5-mark Explain two with a source, (d) 12-mark Evaluate. 3+4+5+12 = 24 per question, 48 for two, plus 3 SPaG = 51. There is no 3-mark Describe.
findings.evidence: spec Paper 4 assessment overview (51 marks, two questions, each (a) to (d)) + command-word table

findings.claim: Question 5 is 'Discuss this statement' / '12 marks - Discuss a Statement'
findings.truth: The 12-mark command word is Evaluate.

findings.claim: Quotations mix Bible translations: Isaiah 53 'wounded for our transgressions' (KJV/RSV; NIV has 'pierced'), Mark 1:1 in the 1984 NIV wording; L2 'clothed and in his right mind' (NIV: 'dressed'); L4 'wishing to satisfy the crowd' (NIV: 'wanting'); L5 'Immediately they left their nets' (NIV: 'At once').
findings.truth: All are genuine renderings in some translation, so no student loses a mark. Worth one pass to settle the unit on NIV if the house standard is NIV.

findings.claim: 'the passage reference earns the fifth mark automatically'
findings.truth: The fifth mark is for referring to a source of wisdom or authority in support of the explanation. A bare reference that supports nothing does not earn it automatically.

findings.claim: "Edexcel's archaic transliteration of Elijah - use 'Elias' in answers, not 'Elijah', when citing spec passages."
findings.truth: Elias and Elijah name the same prophet. The spec uses Elias, but no rule stops a student writing Elijah, and telling them not to is invented exam advice.
findings.evidence: spec 4A section 1.6 uses 'Elias'; no rubric bans 'Elijah'

findings.claim: 'fulfillment' in the question 6 mark scheme
findings.truth: British spelling is 'fulfilment'.

findings.claim: High Priest: 'The Jewish ruling council, also called the Sanhedrin; led by the High Priest...'
findings.truth: The High Priest is a person - the senior Jewish priest who presided over the Sanhedrin. The definition describes the council instead. The same wrong text sits in the content_html data-def.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction: the same lesson calls him 'the High Priest' who 'tears his clothes'

findings.claim: 'this is the first time a human being - not a demon - correctly identifies Jesus with this title while he is alive'
findings.truth: Mark 15:39 places the centurion's words after Jesus has died: he 'saw how he died' and then spoke. The lesson's own flashcard says 'immediately after Jesus died'.

findings.claim: Question 3 mark scheme: 'the first human to correctly identify Jesus during his lifetime is a Gentile Roman soldier'
findings.truth: Same error: the centurion speaks after the death.

findings.claim: 'the scriptural foundation for Christian sacramental practice across all denominations'
findings.truth: Quakers and the Salvation Army do not celebrate the Eucharist. 'Most denominations' is accurate and is a usable evaluation point.

findings.claim: 'In Mark 10:41-45, the disciples argue about which of them is the greatest.'
findings.truth: Mark 10:41 says the ten became indignant with James and John, who had asked to sit at Jesus's right and left. The argument about who is greatest is Mark 9:33-37, a different passage.

findings.claim: 'Flossünbürg concentration camp'
findings.truth: The camp is Flossenburg. The knowledge check in the same lesson spells it correctly, so the lesson contradicts itself.
findings.evidence: Bonhoeffer was executed at Flossenburg, 9 April 1945

findings.claim: Every 12-mark mark scheme uses a four-rung ladder with the board's own mark ranges: 'Mastering (10-12) / Secure (7-9) / Developing (4-6) / Emerging (1-3)'.
findings.truth: The ranges mirror the board's published four-level ladder for the (d) question, which the house copyright rule keeps out of our fields. Options: (a) relabel to the house band vocabulary (Top band / Upper-mid band / Mid band / Lower-mid band / Low band) and drop the numeric ranges, or (b) leave it to the unit-wide band-ladder sweep already queued in the retro programme. Recommend (b) so all 178 ladders change in one consistent pass; the same four rungs appear in all five lessons here.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md copyright distancing; retro programme band-ladder queue

findings.claim: Lesson 3 description is 102 characters and lesson 5's is 108; the house limit is under 100.
findings.truth: Neither is a fact error, so no edit is written. A later edit to either lesson will trip the validator until they are trimmed.

summary: Paper 4 exam form was wrong in all five lessons: seven practice questions used a 3-mark Describe form that does not exist and all five 12-mark questions used Discuss instead of Evaluate. Content errors: Mark 10:41-45 described as the argument about who is greatest (that is Mark 9:33-37), the High Priest glossary entry defining the Sanhedrin, the centurion's confession placed before Jesus's death, Matthew's 'disciples' imported into Mark 14:4, and Flossenburg misspelled.
